Urban planning and development control · Nigerian complaint guidance

Land-use, planning-permission and building-control complaints

Identify the responsible development-control authority and organise evidence about planning approval, construction, land use or demolition concerns.

By PetitionDesk Editorial Team · Reviewed 25 August 2026

Who this guide is for: Residents, property owners or applicants affected by a planning decision, unauthorised construction, land-use conflict or development-control action.

Understand the problem before writing

Planning and development-control responsibilities depend heavily on location. An Abuja construction complaint is not necessarily handled by the same authority as a Lagos building-control dispute or a planning matter in another state. Begin with the property address and the agency that issued, withheld or enforced the relevant decision.

Identify the specific concern: planning approval, building-setback compliance, structural safety, a demolition notice, noise or obstruction arising from construction, a disputed occupancy decision or a land-use change. These issues require different records and should not be merged into a general allegation that a property is illegal.

Preserve application references, official notices, approved drawings where lawfully available, photographs taken safely and communications with the responsible office. If a building appears immediately unsafe, prioritise the relevant emergency and public-safety process rather than waiting for an ordinary administrative complaint.

Property ownership, planning permission and civil possession are related but distinct. A planning authority may investigate compliance while a court, mediator or land registry deals with a separate title or private ownership question.

Build an evidence checklist

Use records that relate directly to your complaint. Put events in date order, identify the organisation involved, and keep copies of every message or acknowledgement. Describe what your documents actually show; do not present an allegation as a proven finding.

  • Exact property address, state and local development area
  • Responsible planning or building-control institution
  • Application, permit, notice or reference number
  • Relevant photographs and dates of the activity
  • Copies of official correspondence or enforcement notices
  • Clear explanation of the safety or administrative concern

Choose the institution that can respond

Contact the planning, development-control or building-safety office responsible for the property's location. Identify whether you seek an inspection, clarification of approval status, review of an enforcement decision or a documented response to a public-safety concern.

A company mentioned in a statement, address, receipt or background document is not automatically the institution responsible for the complaint. Identify who provided the disputed service, who made the decision, and who can supply records or correct the problem.

Decide whether escalation is justified

If the relevant office does not respond, preserve the original application or complaint reference and identify the supervising administrative or complaint authority. Seek legal advice where a demolition, ownership dispute or court order requires urgent or specialist action.

Before escalating, keep the original complaint reference, the institution's written answer where available, and a concise explanation of what remains unresolved. Check the current instructions published by the relevant authority instead of assuming that one deadline applies to every type of complaint.

Worked example: applying the route in practice

A resident reporting a suspected unsafe building in Abuja should state the location, visible condition, dates observed, any prior report and the requested official inspection without claiming to know the builder's permit status.

Avoid common mistakes and protect personal data

Do not publish unverified ownership claims, assume all construction without a visible sign lacks approval or send an FCT planning dispute to a Lagos building authority.

Remove passwords, one-time passcodes, card security codes and unrelated medical, financial or family information. Request a specific remedy supported by your evidence, such as an explanation, correction, investigation, refund or written decision.

Frequently asked questions

Why does the property location matter?

Planning and building-control jurisdiction is linked to the state, Federal Capital Territory or other local authority responsible for the specific site.

Is a planning complaint the same as a land-ownership claim?

No. Planning compliance, title disputes and private possession may require different institutions and procedures.

Official sources and contact starting points

These links point to the organisations' published websites or complaint resources. Check that the channel and procedure remain current before sharing your complaint or evidence.

  • FCT Department of Development Control
  • Lagos State Building Control Agency
